set.approach: The Pigeon Feathers are the shorter spires above the East Creek basin, reached from Applebee Dome or the Kain Hut. This route lies on Wide Awake Tower's south flank, the tower beyond the one holding Solitary Confinement. Walk up the snow gully on that side to the paired corners, one facing left and one facing right, on a pillar, and begin in the flare right under the corner that faces left, using a short pitch to reach the ledge when snow covers it.
set.descent_text: Rappel the route with two ropes. Not every rappel anchor sits at a belay, so note them on the way up; the anchors may need fresh cord.

set.approach: The Pigeon Feathers are the shorter spires above the East Creek basin, reached from Applebee Dome or the Kain Hut. The route climbs Fingerberry Tower and can be seen from the snow arete linking the col between Pigeon and Howser and the East Creek basin. Drop into the scoop below that arete and scramble over boulders and crevasses to the crack system that leads to the big roof higher up.
set.descent_text: Every belay is equipped with rappel hangers, so the route can be rappelled.

set.approach: The Pigeon Feathers are the shorter spires above the East Creek basin, reached from Applebee Dome or the Kain Hut. The climb lies on the ridge under East Peak's north side. Begin slightly left of the buttress toe and left of the big corner system dividing it, under an offwidth in a corner that faces left.
set.descent_text: From the summit, downclimb east along the ridge to slings for a short rappel onto broken ground, from which the Crack of Noon route or a snow descent can be reached.

set.approach: The south-facing routes on Serra 2 begin by hiking uphill from Sunny Knob. The route follows the huge, tangled ridge complex that rises directly above Sunny Knob; low fifth class between snowfields leads to the base of Phantom Tower.
set.descent_text: From the notch below the summit block, rappel down the icy, snowy gully behind the notch on the northeast side to the Upper Tellot Glacier, then cross the glacier to the Plummer Hut.

set.approach: Overlook Mountain is in the Triple Peaks group of the South Powell Divide. Drive up Goat Main to the foot of the Goat 2 forest road and follow it until it bends onto an old bushy road, then find the flagging into open forest on the right. An old trail leads up through dense bush to the south ridge, which begins right where the forest ends.
set.descent_text: Descend the northwest ridge to a key ledge that gives easy access into the bowl below the south ridge, then follow along the ridge back to the bush.

set.approach: It lies in the Skwim Mt area, at the top of the Stillwater main road. Hike up the Skwim trail, climb the boulder field directly, then contour left beneath the Boot to reach the north ridge, then walk the ridge to the base of the route.
set.descent_text: A tree at the top serves as a belay for the second and as a rappel anchor; rappelling is the alternative to the dense, bushy south face route.

set.approach: The Big Scoop Wall is the broad granite basin on the southeast face of Habrich West, reached by Al's Habrich Ridge trail or another trail up the ridge. From Habrich West's summit, descend its south side and curve around toward the wall; the Glenn's Gangway trail also leads to its base. This is the right-most route on the wall. It starts on a smaller horizontal fault on the lower scoop, in a brushy corner beside a tilted dead tree, and a single bolt marks the start.

set.approach: Pull off on the right immediately short of the first tunnel you meet driving east from the Rogers Pass discovery centre. Walk back up the road a short way, cross it, and take the service road to the shed on the far side to the end of the avalanche chute, then follow the chute uphill. The South Tower is the buttress up the Camels' southern side; three tree bands show below it, and pitched climbing starts at a ledge above the third band with orange tat on a tree.
